newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Council ends sanctions against Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: UN Council ends sanctions against Yugoslavia.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council on Tuesday formally ended trade sanctions against the Yugoslav republics of Serbia and Montenegro, first imposed in 1992 for their role in fomenting the war in Bosnia.

Sanctions against Yugoslavia as well as Bosnian Serbs were suspended by the council last November as a followup to their participation in the U.S.-initiated Dayton peace accords. The council at that time stipulated the sanctions would be lifted entirely after this year's Bosnian elections, held on two weeks ago on September 14.
The resolution, approved by a 15-0 vote, "terminates with immediate effect" the May 1992 sanctions that included a stringent trade embargo and a travel and transport ban.
"We regard this as a very good move. It shows that the peace process is on track," said British Ambassador Sir John Weston.

At the insistence of the United States, the document warned, however, that the council would consider re-imposing any of the sanctions if Yugoslavia or the Bosnian Serbs failed "significantly to meet its obligations under the (Dayton) peace agreement." But most diplomats considered it unlikely countries such as Russia would vote to restore any of the embargoes.

However the resolution does not release Belgrade's frozen assets because of disputes and claims from successor states, such as Croatia, Bosnia, Slovenia and Macedonia, after the breakup of the former Yugoslavia. Also held in abeyance will be Yugslavia's re-admittance to the U.N. General Assembly and other bodies in the world organization from which it was suspended because of its disputed legal status.
